concepts.def: Change in concentration of a reactant or product per unit time.
How rate depends on a reactant's concentration (0, 1 or 2).

walkthroughs.body_html:
Rate Equations — a core area of A-Level Chemistry.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Rate Equations brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Rate Equations.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: Which species has the same electron configuration as Ar?
options: Na⁺
Cl⁻
F⁻
Mg²⁺

mcqs.q: Successive ionisation energies of an atom always:
options: Decrease
Stay the same
Increase
Vary randomly

mcqs.q: How does a catalyst speed up a reaction?
options: A catalyst gives extra kinetic energy to the reactant particles.
The order of reaction is always equal to the number of reactants in the equation.
It provides an alternative reaction pathway with a lower activation energy.
A catalyst lowers the activation energy of the original reaction pathway.

mcqs.q: Why does increasing temperature increase the rate of reaction significantly?
options: Particles collide much more frequently at higher temperature, which is the main reason for the rate increase.
Higher temperature increases the concentration of the reactants.
Mainly because a much larger fraction of collisions have energy at least equal to the activation energy; collision frequency increases only slightly.
A catalyst gives extra kinetic energy to the reactant particles.

mcqs.q: Can you determine the order of a reaction with respect to a reactant from the balanced equation?
options: No — orders must be determined experimentally; they often differ from the stoichiometric coefficients.
The order of reaction is always equal to the number of reactants in the equation.
Higher temperature increases the concentration of the reactants.
The order of reaction with respect to each reactant equals its coefficient in the balanced equation.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Relative atomic mass”?
options: Number of protons in the nucleus, which determines the element's identity.
Weighted mean mass of an atom relative to 1/12 of the mass of a ¹²C atom.
Atoms of the same element with the same Z but different numbers of neutrons.
Energy to remove one mole of electrons from one mole of gaseous atoms (or ions): X(g) → X⁺(g) + e⁻.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Atomic number Z”?
options: Number of protons in the nucleus, which determines the element's identity.
Weighted mean mass of an atom relative to 1/12 of the mass of a ¹²C atom.
Distribution of electrons across s, p, d and f subshells, filling lowest energy first.
Total number of protons and neutrons in the nucleus.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Electron configuration”?
options: Atoms of the same element with the same Z but different numbers of neutrons.
Total number of protons and neutrons in the nucleus.
Distribution of electrons across s, p, d and f subshells, filling lowest energy first.
Number of protons in the nucleus, which determines the element's identity.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Ionisation energy”?
options: Atoms of the same element with the same Z but different numbers of neutrons.
Energy to remove one mole of electrons from one mole of gaseous atoms (or ions): X(g) → X⁺(g) + e⁻.
Total number of protons and neutrons in the nucleus.
Number of protons in the nucleus, which determines the element's identity.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Isotope”?
options: Weighted mean mass of an atom relative to 1/12 of the mass of a ¹²C atom.
Number of protons in the nucleus, which determines the element's identity.
Atoms of the same element with the same Z but different numbers of neutrons.
Total number of protons and neutrons in the nucleus.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Mass number A”?
options: Total number of protons and neutrons in the nucleus.
Atoms of the same element with the same Z but different numbers of neutrons.
Energy to remove one mole of electrons from one mole of gaseous atoms (or ions): X(g) → X⁺(g) + e⁻.
Weighted mean mass of an atom relative to 1/12 of the mass of a ¹²C atom.
